title: Brilliant: Brilliant FAQ
observation: Math and coding learning through visual models, hands-on problems and a digital tutor. Documented features: Interactive problem solving, Immediate feedback, Learning paths, Koji tutor, Web, iOS and Android, Progress sync. Official FAQ says lessons require an internet connection and are not available offline.
provenance_notes: Vendor FAQ reviewed; no hands-on audit. No efficacy multiplier from the marketing page is treated as verified research. Not normalized; no comparable Australia-specific checkout quote obtained.
job_to_be_done: Use limited time to understand, retain or apply useful knowledge.
inference: Brainbuilder cannot claim interactive short learning or guided tutoring as unique. Offline continuity is a possible comparison dimension to test against this product, not against the whole market.
willingness_to_pay: Not measured. Competitor availability is not willingness-to-pay evidence.
negative_evidence: The documented features challenge a hypothesis that microlearning, audio, quizzes or source intake alone would differentiate Brainbuilder.

title: Blinkist: Blinkist Pricing: Compare Premium & PRO Plans

segment: Book and podcast summaries, source summarization
job_to_be_done: Use limited time to understand, retain or apply useful knowledge.

title: Headway: What is Headway?
observation: Personal growth through key ideas from nonfiction books. Documented features: 15-minute text and audio summaries, Daily insights and widgets, Streaks, Personal recommendations, Curated collections, Spaced repetition. Text/audio choice and a daily habit are explicit parts of the documented product.
provenance_notes: Official help page last updated 2025-06-17 and retrieved in November 2026. Feature outcomes and retention effectiveness were not independently measured. Not verified in comparable currency/platform; omitted.
job_to_be_done: Use limited time to understand, retain or apply useful knowledge.
inference: A daily lesson plus streak plus spaced repetition is already a directly marketed bundle. Brainbuilder needs a more concrete audience/outcome and better execution of the daily learning loop.
willingness_to_pay: Not measured. Competitor availability is not willingness-to-pay evidence.
negative_evidence: The documented features challenge a hypothesis that microlearning, audio, quizzes or source intake alone would differentiate Brainbuilder.

job_to_be_done: Use limited time to understand, retain or apply useful knowledge.

willingness_to_pay: Not measured. Competitor availability is not willingness-to-pay evidence.
negative_evidence: The documented features challenge a hypothesis that microlearning, audio, quizzes or source intake alone would differentiate Brainbuilder.

title: RemNote: Your AI Tutor: Learn Any PDF to Mastery
observation: A guided AI learning system for study materials, with a strong exam/study framing. Documented features: 5–10-minute guided sections from PDFs, Summaries, Spaced repetition flashcards, Multiple-choice and free-response quizzes, Recall and application question modes, Per-topic mastery tracking, Explanations and tutor responses with source citations. The feature page links mobile apps; this scan did not independently test guided learning on mobile or offline behavior.
provenance_notes: Vendor page's '100% mastery' language is not treated as proof of durable competence. No direct usability or delayed-retention comparison performed. Not verified in comparable currency/platform; omitted.
job_to_be_done: Use limited time to understand, retain or apply useful knowledge.
inference: Source grounding, adaptive follow-up questions, application questions and topic tracking are already explicit capabilities. The remaining opportunity must be validated at the audience, routine and outcome level.
willingness_to_pay: Not measured. Competitor availability is not willingness-to-pay evidence.
negative_evidence: The documented features challenge a hypothesis that microlearning, audio, quizzes or source intake alone would differentiate Brainbuilder.

title: Roediger and Karpicke (2006), Test-Enhanced Learning
observation: In experiments with prose passages, restudying was better on an immediate test, while prior free-recall testing produced better retention at delayed tests of two days or one week.
provenance_notes: Publication month: 2006-03. DOI: 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2006.01693.x. Full abstract text was read; full paper was not read. The study does not validate this app, AI grading, all subject types, or learning while multitasking. Abstract reviewed; no app-specific effect size inferred.
job_to_be_done: Recall and use previously learned information after a delay.
inference: Include a brief attempt to recall before revealing an explanation; measure delayed recall instead of treating reading or listening completion as mastery.
willingness_to_pay: Not a market-demand or pricing study.
negative_evidence: No direct evidence here for Brainbuilder effectiveness, on-the-go multitasking, voice UX, ideal lesson duration, or willingness to pay.

title: Cepeda, Vul, Rohrer, Wixted and Pashler (2008), Spacing Effects in Learning
observation: The study varied review intervals and later testing delays. The interval associated with best retention changed with the desired retention period; simply increasing spacing indefinitely did not keep improving performance.
provenance_notes: Publication month: 2008-11. DOI: 10.1111/j.1467-9280.2008.02209.x. Full abstract text was read; full paper was not read. Fact-learning study; not proof that a particular app algorithm, notification schedule, or fixed lesson duration is optimal. Abstract reviewed.
job_to_be_done: Recall and use previously learned information after a delay.
inference: Return to previous material after time has passed, using evidence of recall and the user's goal to adapt scheduling. Display what needs practice without claiming one universal schedule is optimal.
willingness_to_pay: Not a market-demand or pricing study.
negative_evidence: No direct evidence here for Brainbuilder effectiveness, on-the-go multitasking, voice UX, ideal lesson duration, or willingness to pay.

title: Butler (2010), Repeated testing produces superior transfer of learning relative to repeated studying
observation: Four experiments found better later retention and performance on new inferential questions after repeated testing than repeated study, including tested questions across knowledge domains.
provenance_notes: Publication month: 2010-09. DOI: 10.1037/a0019902. Full abstract text was read; full paper was not read. Controlled text-learning experiments and a one-week test. Not proof of workplace performance, broad expertise, or far transfer in every domain. University-hosted original abstract reviewed.
job_to_be_done: Recall and use previously learned information after a delay.
inference: Use a fresh scenario or explain-in-your-own-words task to check application, rather than counting repeated recognition of the same answer as full understanding.
willingness_to_pay: Not a market-demand or pricing study.
negative_evidence: No direct evidence here for Brainbuilder effectiveness, on-the-go multitasking, voice UX, ideal lesson duration, or willingness to pay.
